presentation.summary: A deliberately low, owner-only 1200 meter floor for the exact governed 12-minute walk/run test, separated from laboratory VO2 and population fitness categories.

authority_basis.numeric_value_explanation: The 1200 meter value is an AGAS engineering prior corresponding to an average 6 km/h pace. It is not extracted from the Mayorga-Vega meta-analysis and is not a validated health, performance, or safety threshold.
authority_basis.operational_use_explanation: A planning reviewer may provisionally adopt the value only for the owner-alpha athlete and the exact governed 12-minute distance estimate. The validity evidence supports the field measure, not this threshold.

governs: One owner-alpha comparison between a current estimate from the exact governed 12-minute walk/run protocol and a provisional 1200 meter floor.
A below-floor result may support an aerobic-capacity development need while retaining the observation, estimate, floor, evidence, and judgment-authority identities.
does_not_establish: A population norm, percentile, diagnosis, cardiovascular-risk threshold, running-readiness threshold, or medical clearance.
That 1200 meters is a scientific minimum, public-health target, or optimal target for this athlete.
A training modality, weekly minutes, intensity, progression rule, or permission to exercise.
That meeting the floor proves adequate aerobic fitness or eliminates the value of maintenance and later personal calibration.
unresolved_limitations: No reviewed scientific source validates 1200 meters as a minimum useful competency for the owner-alpha athlete.
Test performance depends on pacing, motivation, route accuracy, surface, weather, footwear, fatigue, and walking or running familiarity.
The meta-analysis supports criterion-related validity of the field test but not a universal or owner-specific cutoff.
The threshold should be replaced or withdrawn after repeatable personal baseline and response observations exist.

evidence.title: Mayorga-Vega et al. (2016), walk/run field-test validity meta-analysis
evidence.population: Children, adolescents, and adults represented across 123 criterion-validity studies.
evidence.finding: Distance in the 12-minute walk/run test had a pooled validity correlation of 0.78 with criterion cardiorespiratory-fitness measures.
limitations: The review does not validate 1200 meters as an AGAS floor.
A field-test distance is not a direct laboratory VO2 measurement.
Heterogeneous samples and protocols limit athlete-specific transfer.
evidence.conflict_disclosure: The authors declared no competing interests.

source.title: Criterion-Related Validity of the Distance- and Time-Based Walk/Run Field Tests for Estimating Cardiorespiratory Fitness: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
provenance_notes: Title, authors, journal, publication date, identifiers, study count, pooled correlation, and conflict statement were checked against PubMed and the full PMC article.
The abstract is intentionally not copied into the stored snapshot.
This release uses the review to support the validity of the 12-minute walk/run distance as an aerobic field measure, not to authorize a VO2 conversion, competency floor, or training dose.

claim.claim: Across the studies synthesized by Mayorga-Vega and colleagues, distance covered during the 12-minute walk/run test had high criterion-related validity for estimating cardiorespiratory fitness; the pooled correlation was 0.78 with a 95% confidence interval from 0.72 to 0.83.
claim.population: Children, adolescents, and adults represented across 123 included studies; the 12-minute walk/run result pooled the applicable validation samples.
claim.intervention: A 12-minute field test in which the participant walks or runs to cover the greatest possible distance.
claim.comparator: Laboratory criterion measures of cardiorespiratory fitness in the included validation studies.
claim.outcome: Criterion-related validity of test distance for estimating cardiorespiratory fitness.
claim.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of criterion-related validity studies
claim.effect_direction: Greater valid distance generally corresponds to higher cardiorespiratory fitness.
claim.uncertainty: The pooled association does not make field distance a direct VO2 measurement, does not remove effort and pacing effects, and does not establish an owner-specific floor.
limitations: The included samples, protocols, surfaces, criterion tests, and participant ages were heterogeneous.
A high correlation still leaves individual estimation error and does not establish interchangeability with laboratory testing.
The review does not validate an AGAS competency threshold, reassessment interval, or exercise prescription.
claim.applicability_notes: The adult validation literature is directionally applicable to an apparently healthy owner-alpha adult, but current readiness, walking/running familiarity, environment, pacing, and repeat-test consistency remain controlling.
claim.reviewer: Codex evidence synthesis candidate; authority pending

evidence_review_content.source_verification_rationale: The PubMed record and full PMC article for PMID 26987118 were checked for source identity, eligibility, test grouping, pooled 12-minute walk/run correlation, confidence interval, and declared competing interests.
evidence_review_content.extraction_rationale: The claim retains the validity association for the exact field-test family while explicitly excluding conversion into a floor.
evidence_review_content.evidence_strength_rationale: Moderate reflects a systematic review and meta-analysis of validation studies, reduced from high for heterogeneous populations, comparators, protocols, and individual prediction error.
evidence_review_content.applicability_rationale: Moderate reflects adult evidence and practical owner-alpha feasibility without assuming the pooled samples exactly match this athlete.
evidence_review_content.uncertainty: Pacing, motivation, route accuracy, conditions, fatigue, and modality familiarity can materially affect repeatability and transfer.
evidence_review_content.conflict_disclosure: The authors declared no competing interests.

authority.statement: For the owner-alpha athlete only, treat 1200.0 meters under the exact governed 12-minute walk/run protocol as a provisional minimum useful repeat-performance floor.
authority.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; recreationally trained adult doing physical work.
authority.rationale: Twelve hundred meters corresponds to a six kilometer-per-hour average and is a deliberately low sentinel intended to identify a clearly limited result without turning a population association into athlete truth.
authority.applicability_notes: Use only with a current estimate from the matching governed protocol after its separate readiness and environment gates are satisfied. Review after repeat personal measurements exist.
authority.uncertainty: No scientific source validates 1200 meters as a minimum useful athletic competency, and a first personal result cannot establish whether this threshold is appropriately calibrated.
limitations: This threshold has no population-validity claim.
It cannot establish medical safety, running readiness, injury risk, or a training dose.
Meeting it does not show that aerobic capacity is optimal or should be ignored.
Personal longitudinal calibration should replace it when enough observations exist.
authority.authored_by: AGAS engineering candidate prepared by Codex
authority.qualification_context: System engineering synthesis; not user-authored and not a claim of a licensed clinical or conditioning credential. A planning reviewer must explicitly adopt the exact judgment before operational use.

authority_review_content.attestation: I adopt this exact owner-alpha product judgment for narrow planning use and understand that 1200 meters is not a scientific finding, population norm, safety clearance, or exercise prescription.
authority_review_content.uncertainty: Approval does not establish external validity; replace or withdraw this authority when personal calibration or better applicable evidence supports a different decision.

floor.population: Owner-only alpha; age 30 to 39; exact governed 12-minute walk/run protocol.
floor.applicability_notes: Compare only with a current estimate from the matching governed protocol. Use the result as one planning input; never as diagnosis, safety clearance, or a universal aerobic-capacity judgment.
floor.uncertainty: The threshold is an explicit AGAS engineering judgment supported by assessment-validity context but no numeric scientific validation. It is provisional and replaceable after personal calibration.

floor_review_content.applicability_rationale: Approve only for the owner-alpha athlete, ages 30 to 39, after a current estimate from the exact governed 12-minute walk/run protocol. The comparison may inform development or maintenance but is not a medical or safety decision.
floor_review_content.uncertainty: The source supports the field measure only; the number 1200 does not come from it. Approval adopts the separate reviewed engineering authority and requires later personal calibration.

release.release_rationale: Provide one honest, owner-reviewable aerobic-capacity floor so the governed 12-minute distance can enter planning without a VO2 conversion or disguising a product judgment as a scientific norm.
release.release_uncertainty: Ratification would authorize only this owner-alpha comparison. It creates no diagnosis, universal norm, readiness clearance, adaptation priority, exercise selection, duration dose, session, or permission to train.
